name: Gambia
snapshot: Mainland Africa's smallest country, a sliver along the Gambia River, where Adama Barrow is seeking a third term in the 5 December 2026 election.
culture: The Gambia is a ribbon of land on both banks of its river, almost entirely surrounded by Senegal, with which it shares Wolof, Mandinka and Fula culture. Griots, hereditary praise singers and historians, play the kora, a 21-string harp-lute. Kunta Kinteh Island, linked to the story of Alex Haley's "Roots", draws heritage visitors from the African diaspora.
society: Tourism, groundnuts and remittances drive the economy, and many young Gambians attempt the dangerous "back way" to Europe. Unemployment is high. A truth commission documented the killings and torture of Yahya Jammeh's 22-year rule, and a special court with ECOWAS is being set up to try abuses.
situation: Adama Barrow defeated the dictator Yahya Jammeh in 2016; Jammeh left for exile only after a regional military intervention. Barrow won again in 2021 after breaking with the coalition that had backed him on a promise to serve three years. He is running for a third term in December 2026, and several opposition parties have united behind a single challenger.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected by simple plurality for five-year terms and heads the government; attempts to adopt a new constitution with term limits failed in 2020 and 2024.

story: A sliver of land along the Gambia River that Britain held while France took the surrounding Senegal. Independent in 1965, it was a rare democracy under Dawda Jawara until Yahya Jammeh seized power in 1994 and ruled with terror for 22 years. In 2016 he lost an election to Adama Barrow and was forced into exile when West African troops moved in.
